findings.title: The opening description uses unnecessary technical language
findings.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
findings.why: Several of these words are unfamiliar, and they make a simple family activity sound complicated and artificial.

findings.title: Exact hardcover prices are not shown on the landing page
findings.evidence: The page says “See pricing” and “Printed hardcovers shipped across the UK” but gives no price.
findings.why: I need to understand the cost before becoming committed, although the separate Pricing link makes it reasonable to check.

findings.title: The decorative image has no description
findings.evidence: The image beside the opening text is shown as “image (no description)”.
findings.why: A meaningful description would make the example understandable if I were using a screen reader or could not see the image.

findings.title: Email and password fields have no visible labels
findings.evidence: Items [5] and [6] are described as textboxes with no label; only the placeholders say “Email” and “Password.”
findings.why: I can understand the placeholders, but the labels disappear while I type and may not be clear to people using assistive technology.

findings.title: Footer text has very weak contrast
findings.evidence: The links “Privacy,” “Terms,” “Contact,” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” are shown in extremely pale grey.
findings.why: I need comfortably readable text, especially on a laptop, and the footer words are difficult for me to see.

findings.title: Unexplained technical profile-sync error
findings.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
findings.why: I cannot tell whether my account is safe, whether the problem is temporary, or whether I need to do something. If I have done something wrong, I would want a plain explanation and a way to fix it.

findings.title: The dashboard greets the account name rather than the person's name
findings.evidence: “Welcome back, Demo”
findings.why: It feels impersonal and makes me briefly question whether I have reached the correct account.

findings.title: Footer text has weak contrast and is very small
findings.evidence: The “Privacy,” “Terms,” “Contact,” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” footer text appears faint and undersized.
findings.why: I can barely read the privacy and terms links, and these are particularly important to me before sharing family details.

findings.title: Footer text has very low contrast
findings.evidence: The footer links 'Privacy', 'Terms' and 'Contact', together with '© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.', are extremely pale grey on an off-white background.
findings.why: I can hardly read these links, and I may need to enlarge the page to inspect the privacy and terms information.

findings.title: Relationship is preselected without an explanation
findings.evidence: [11] shows 'Grandparent' already selected, although no relationship has yet been entered.
findings.why: It happens to be correct for Grandma Maggie, but I would like to know that I must still check it rather than assume the site has understood the form.

findings.title: Footer links are very low contrast
findings.evidence: “Privacy”, “Terms”, and “Contact” in the footer are very pale grey
findings.why: I may need the privacy information and struggle to read these links, especially with my eyesight.

findings.title: Lexile ranges are unexplained
findings.evidence: The page labels the choices “Lexile BR–200L,” “Lexile 200L–500L,” “Lexile 500L–800L,” and “Lexile 800L+.”
findings.why: I want a book Oliver can enjoy, but I need to understand what the numbers mean before choosing.

findings.title: The default reading level may be too advanced for Oliver
findings.evidence: “Lexile 200L–500L” is already checked, even though Oliver is five and the requested reading age is five.
findings.why: If I overlook the setting, the finished book may contain words that are too difficult for him.

findings.title: No plain-language explanation of how an uploaded photo is handled
findings.evidence: “Upload a clear photo of your child's face so the illustrations look like them.” No nearby text explains whether the original photo is kept, whether faces are copied, or who can see it.
findings.why: I am cautious about uploading a child's photograph, and without a reason and privacy explanation I would probably avoid it altogether.

findings.title: File control has no explicit visible label
findings.evidence: [30] file-upload (no label), although the browser button reads “Choose File” and the heading says “Add a photo (optional).”
findings.why: “Choose File” by itself does not explain what kind of file is wanted, although the surrounding text makes the purpose reasonably clear.

findings.title: The loading state has no explanatory text
findings.evidence: The page shows only a circular loading indicator and no message such as “Creating Oliver’s book.”
findings.why: I cannot tell whether my request worked, and I may assume that I have done something wrong.

findings.title: No way to cancel or leave the loading process
findings.evidence: There is no “Cancel,” “Back,” or “Continue later” control on the loading page.
findings.why: If the process takes too long, I feel trapped and have no clear way to regain control.

findings.title: Very pale footer text
findings.evidence: The footer items “Privacy,” “Terms,” “Contact,” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” are extremely faint against the background.
findings.why: The low contrast makes the small text difficult for me to read.

findings.title: The title contains a spelling error
findings.evidence: The heading says “The Magical Adventrue of Oliver” and the cover repeats “The Magical Adventrue of Oliver.”
findings.why: This is intended to become a treasured present for a five-year-old, so an obvious spelling mistake on the cover makes the book feel cheap and not ready to give.

findings.title: The selected illustration style was not followed
findings.evidence: The earlier choice was “soft watercolour,” but the generated page says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic” and the cover has a flat, simple cartoon style.
findings.why: I made a deliberate choice about the look of Oliver’s book, and changing it without explanation makes me feel that the website has not respected my instructions.

findings.title: The generated cover omits important personal details
findings.evidence: The cover shows “Oliver,” a farmhouse, and a blue kite, but not his brown curly hair, freckles, green wellies, Grandma Maggie, or the kite’s connection to Grandpa’s shirt.
findings.why: I want this to feel like a story about my family, not a generic child and a kite. The missing details may be explained later in the pages, but the cover does not make the family connection clear.

findings.title: The next-page control is not described
findings.evidence: The only visible page navigation is a small button labelled “›,” with “1 / 9” shown below the book.
findings.why: I can probably work out what the arrow means, but a written label would be clearer and more reassuring when I am reading carefully.

findings.title: Premium gift wrap is selected by default
findings.evidence: [6] “Premium gift wrap” is checked, with “£7.99” added to the total.
findings.why: I did not ask for gift wrap, and I am cautious about extra charges. Its pre-selection makes me wonder what other options or terms may be hidden below.

findings.title: The cost rises sharply through shipping and the added option
findings.evidence: “Hardcover: The Magical Adventure of Oliver £24.99,” followed by “Premium gift wrap £7.99,” “Shipping & handling £12.99,” and “Total £45.97.”
findings.why: I would like to know before entering my address that the base £24.99 book will actually cost £45.97, and the page does not explain why shipping is so high.

findings.title: Timed reservation may create unnecessary pressure
findings.evidence: “Your price is reserved for 09:57.”
findings.why: A countdown makes me feel hurried just as I am trying to understand the order and avoid mistakes.

findings.title: Payment security and delivery terms are not visible before entering details
findings.evidence: The visible checkout shows card fields, while “Privacy” and “Terms” are below the fold; no payment-security statement is shown near the fields.
findings.why: Before giving financial details, I want to know who handles them, whether the connection is secure, what cancellation rights apply, and when my card would be charged.

findings.title: Sparse address field may be unsuitable for UK delivery
findings.evidence: [7] is a single textbox labelled only “Address,” even though the service is described as UK-delivered.
findings.why: A single box may still work, but I cannot tell whether it expects the entire address or separate address lines.

findings.title: coherence

findings.title: emotional_resonance
